newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates fall for sixth week to 9-month low.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates fall for sixth week to 9-month low.

text.p: Fixed-rate home mortgage rates fell for the sixth week in a row and hit a nine-month low this week, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Wednesday.

Thirty-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 7.52 percent in the week ending Nov. 29, down from 7.53 percent last week. The rate has not been lower since the week ended March 8, when the average was 7.38 percent.
Fifteen-year loans also fell a sixth consecutive week to an average 7.04 percent, the lowest since a rate of 6.87 percent in the March 8 week. Last week's 15-year rate averaged 7.06 percent.
Last week's rates were also the lowest since the March 8 week.
Adjustable mortgage rates inched up to 5.50 percent from 5.48 percent last week.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.33 percent, the 15-year 6.85 percent, and the adjustable loan 5.60 percent.

"With 30-year fixed-rate mortgages settling around 7.5 percent, we anticipate that the ARM percentage of home purchases will begin to decline from its year-round high of 33 percent," Frank Nothaft, Freddie Mac deputy chief economist, said.
"We have generally found that families prefer the certainty of a fixed-rate mortgage when interest rates are as low as they are today."
On Monday the National Assocation of Realtors said U.S. October sales of existing homes fell 1.5 percent to a 3.97 million unit annual rate.
Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average of 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans, 1.7 percent on 15-year loans, and 1.4 percent on adjustable mortgages, all unchanged from last week.
